findings.line: Human interrupt resume rules; HumanInterruptV1 (~321-385) vs Step 2 RouteSegmentStateV1
findings.scenario: A propose-class skill hits an interrupt while the segment is active. Step 2 allows only active -> completed|failed|cancelled|budget-exhausted and treats terminals as final. Step 3 says the control plane 'suspends the segment without advancing authority' and an approval 'resumes the same segment'. There is no interrupted/suspended CAS state, no stop-work rule, and no legal resume transition. Implementers must either leave the segment active (driver/worker can continue) or terminalize it (resume of the same frozen segment is impossible).
findings.remediation: Add a closed `interrupted` segment state with CAS: active -> interrupted (cancel in-flight work, no proposal/apply, reservation held); interrupted -> active only when HumanDecisionV1 accepts and interrupt/intent/route/context/skill/tool/budget/deadline/expected-state hashes still equal; interrupted -> cancelled|rejected on reject/expiry/mismatch. Forbid resume from any terminal state.

findings.scenario: A skill/worker emits HumanInterruptV1 whose requestedDecisionSchemaHash is a skill-owned schema such as {run_shell: yes|no} or {grant_tool: X}. A named human selects yes. Resume checks that route/context/skill/tool/budget *fields* still match, so no new segment is created, but decisionValue is then interpreted as extra capability. Interrupt has no issuer/actor field, so the model/skill/worker can choose the schema and safeSummary.
findings.remediation: Only the control plane may create HumanInterruptV1. Bind requestedDecisionSchemaHash to a ONE BOX-owned closed vocabulary (e.g. accept-proposal|reject|cancel) that cannot add tools, paths, data classes, budget, or authority. Require control-plane issuer identity; reject skill/worker/provider-authored interrupts. Derive safeSummary only from typed proposal fields.

findings.scenario: After reservation, an invocation is created with the reserved segmentId/budgetReservationId but a different skillAdmissionHash, routePolicyHash, contextBundleHash, or effectiveToolGrantHash than the frozen RouteSegmentIntentV1/ManifestV1. Only budgetReservationId 'must match'. That is an in-place skill/route/context/tool change on a reserved segment and lets a slash draft or child call escape the admitted SkillSetV1.
findings.remediation: Require invocation.segmentManifestHash to equal the reserved manifest for (jobId, segmentId); skillAdmissionHash ∈ that segment's SkillSetV1; routePolicyHash, contextBundleHash, and effectiveToolGrantHash equal the frozen segment hashes (effective tools may only be a recorded intersection subset). Mismatch fails closed and emits no invocation receipt.

findings.scenario: A prior-output, evidence, or project-artifact fragment is stored with authorityClass `policy` or `skill-instruction`. Prose says layers stay separate, but the schema does not bind sourceKind to authorityClass, so quoted instructions can be packed as system/skill authority and change route/tool/approval behavior.
findings.remediation: Close a sourceKind→authorityClass map: accepted-policy→policy; actor-task→human-task; human-decision→human-decision; skill-instruction→skill-instruction; project-artifact|evidence|prior-receipt|prior-output→untrusted-data. Reject any other pair before packing.

findings.scenario: Fragments listed in policy/task/decision arrays may appear 'at most once' in materialization and may be moved to excludedFragmentReceipts while the bundle still validates. Overflow can drop policy/human layers or omit included hashes without a rejected context receipt, so packing is not fail-closed or deterministic.
findings.remediation: Every hash in an authority-class list must appear exactly once in orderedMaterializationHashes. Policy, human-task, and human-decision fragments are mandatory; excluding them invalidates the bundle. Overflow of any remaining fragment returns only a rejected context receipt, never a valid under-cap bundle. Count materialization separators/labels inside actualBytes.

findings.scenario: Criterion requires owner kill switches for skills and slash commands. SlashCommandEntryV1 has owners and admission but no killSwitchRef. A killed skill still leaves an enabled command name parseable; disabling the command requires a healthy registry write, which the skill kill switch is defined to avoid.
findings.remediation: Add command-registry and per-entry ONE BOX killSwitchRef that reject parse and invocation without reading skill bytes. Disabled/killed skillAdmissionHash must make every bound command name/alias fail before grammar success.

findings.scenario: Two currently authorized humans can each write a valid HumanDecisionV1 for the same interruptHash (accept vs reject) because the interrupt record has no state/CAS and no single-assignment rule. Resume can observe the accept and continue the proposed effect.
findings.remediation: Make interrupt single-assignment via CAS: at most one schema-valid decision binds; later decisions fail validation. Resume must use that unique decisionHash.

findings.scenario: Acyclicity forbids the envelope from referencing the final segment receipt. Terminal prose says non-completed states are not apply-eligible, but apply is not required to find a completed RouteSegmentReceiptV1 whose proposalEnvelopeHash equals this envelope (and whose foundation job receipt is the frozen owner). A failed/cancelled/stray envelope can be submitted to the guarded apply path. Failed-bullet text also only bans proposals for ambiguous execution, not all non-completed states.
findings.remediation: Apply eligibility = completed RouteSegmentReceiptV1 with matching proposalEnvelopeHash, schema-valid propose-only envelope, and foundationJobReceiptHash from the frozen job contract. All non-completed terminal combinations must reject proposalEnvelopeHash/output that is apply-shaped. Keep the envelope from hashing the segment receipt.

findings.scenario: Owner arrays may be empty. Acceptance requires owner-bound supply-chain entries; an unowned fixture-only skill/command can still parse, enter a skill set, and produce invocation intents.
findings.remediation: Fail validation unless at least one current OwnerAssignmentV1 is bound and unexpired for each skill and command. Unowned, expired, or revoked refs cannot admit, parse, or invoke.

findings.scenario: Composer payload `/foo\n/bar args` does not match 'one /, one name, then EOS or one ASCII space', but the contract never says the entire payload is a single parse. A line-splitting UI can dispatch two skill-selection drafts from one submit, including pasted/model text that the 'only explicit actor action' rule meant to block.
findings.remediation: Parse the full composer payload as exactly one invocation; any additional command-shaped line or extra leading / fails the whole action. Pasted/retrieved/model text cannot start a parse even if the actor hits send unless the actor also used the explicit command control, not free text.

findings.scenario: Command and skill schemas are independent. User text is 'subject to the skill input schema' after a command parse that used a narrower schema. A future skill schema that accepts paths/URLs/flags can receive those bytes as one field and treat them as execution input while slash grammar claims it never splits to path/URL/shell.
findings.remediation: Require command inputSchemaHash to equal the bound skill inputSchemaHash or to be a closed restriction of it. Skill schemas in this packet cannot admit filesystem paths, URL fetch, shell tokens, or plugin IDs as executable fields.

audit.proof_assessment: Proof is prose planning plus Step 2/TM-05/supply-chain/authorization docs, not an executable oracle. Those sources support deny-by-default tools, no live provider, and no P180 implementation auth, but they do not close Step 3 invariants that are only narrated: interrupt state, decision vocabulary, invocation-to-segment equality, sourceKind↔authorityClass, and apply gating. Treat the markdown as evidence of intent; it does not yet satisfy the completeness predicate.
residual_risks: Future child skill receipts can cycle if children hash parents; first slice has zero children but the receipt rule only forbids referencing the final segment receipt.
HumanInterruptV1.safeSummary remains an attacker-influenced social-engineering channel even with a closed decision enum.
Composer bidi/homoglyph display can spoof slash names while ASCII parse stays closed.
freshnessPolicyRef could encode never-expire and fail open on staleness.
Implementations may treat completed RouteSegmentReceiptV1 as a second job-terminal authority despite foundationJobReceiptHash.
ContextFragmentV1.normalizedBytes is named like content, not a count; storing bytes would put payload into hash-chained control-plane records.
No accessibility contract for pre-dispatch included/excluded source disclosure.
SkillInvocationReceiptV1 terminal states are not a closed enum with the same non-completed proposal ban.
